2 · Alternative suggestions for interactivity

Reply by number: Agree or Change.

  1. S1
    Group the 19 screens into 7 scenes, with the CIDP journey (screens 9–17) as one scene: the journey map stays on screen as the navigation and each stage has the same layers. Appendix A.
  2. S2
    One short scored question per journey stage, as outline V3 (26 Oct, opening section) set out, alongside the reflective picks. Wording from the writer or the stakeholder.
  3. S3
    A payoff after each ranking: a line on how the faculty or the evidence sees it, so the no right answer screens close with something to take away, without storing anyone's answers.
  4. S4
    Screens 11 and 15: the learner picks a challenge, but the same content shows whichever is picked. Either one tailored line per challenge, or a plain reveal.
  5. S5
    The summary (screen 18) replays the learner's own picks and rankings beside the take-home messages. This needs the journey and the summary in one build.
  6. S6
    Mimics: a short question in stage 1 on conditions that could be confused with CIDP (mimics are named on screen 11).
  7. S7
    A one-select confidence check at the start and the end, so the activity can show a change. Optional.
  8. S8
    Plain language and glossary pop-ups for readers with English as a second language (China, Japan). Abbreviations and citation numbers open on select; the look-and-feel options show how on the sample screens. The client's lexicon has a ready glossary (active disease, inadequate response, residual disability, remission).
  9. S9
    How-to screen: time to complete; device-neutral wording (select, not click or hover); the screen 7 ordering task and the rankings work by selecting as well as dragging, for phones and keyboards.

Look and build

  1. S10
    One icon family: storyboard v1 (11 Nov) mixes filled icons, outlines and 3D illustrations. Line icons in round badges throughout, keeping the two-pager's peach (challenge) and lilac (application) coding; illustrations only on the biomarker timeline. See the look-and-feel options.
  2. S11
    Look: four options attached. Forged Frameworks recommends D, touchNEUROLOGY with the brief's journey wave; C if the client wants visible Sanofi alignment.
  3. S12
    Build: one HTML activity, embedded once, so the summary can see the learner's choices and phones and accessibility are handled once. Fallback: Visme for the simple screens with one HTML embed for the journey and summary.

3 · Questions

Reply by number. For the content points: Keep, Change or Drop.

Build and look

  1. Q1
    Branding. Is client branding permitted on the activity, or does it carry the touchNEUROLOGY look with a sponsorship line, as on Unravelling CIDP: Exploring the Role of Complement in Axonal Integrity? If client branding is wanted: the brand pack. In either case: the Sanofi Sans web-font files, which option D would use first.
  2. Q2
    Two-pager imagery. The VML two-pager (7 Jul) is marked Do not photograph, copy or distribute. May its journey wave, icons or background videos be reused or redrawn for the activity?
  3. Q3
    PNS 2026 symposium deck. Two comments on outline V3 screen 5 (12 and 19 Oct) say its list and timeline follow slides 20 and 22 of the PNS 2026 presentation. In storyboard v1 (11 Nov) this is screen 8. The deck is not in the shared folder. Could it be shared?
  4. Q4
    Translation. The target countries include China, Germany and Japan. Is a translated version planned? It changes how the screens are built (text kept out of images, room for longer lines).

Content (for the writer and the medical reviewers)

  1. C1
    Scored questions. Outline V3 (26 Oct, opening section) says multiple-choice questions come at the next stage, with a worked example (correct answer and rationale); a comment there (19 Oct) asked reviewers which screens to focus on. In storyboard v1 (11 Nov), screens 6 and 7 are scored; the journey screens (10–17) are reveals, open picks and rankings. Did the client name screens?
  2. C2
    Screen 12, complement inhibitors. Listed among treatments in storyboard v1 (11 Nov). Sanofi stopped the riliprubart MOBILIZE phase 3 study on 10 June 2026. Please confirm the intended wording with the medical reviewers.
  3. C3
    Screen 7, order of variants. In storyboard v1 (11 Nov), focal and multifocal are both ≤15%, so put the five variants in order has a tie. Which order is correct?
  4. C4
    Sanofi CIDP lexicon (October 2026 FINAL). Wording in storyboard v1 (11 Nov) that departs from the client's language guide (table in appendix B), for example non-responding (avoid; inadequate response preferred) and patients (people living with CIDP preferred).
  5. C5
    Small points in storyboard v1 (11 Nov). Title wording differs from the approved V3 title (26 Oct); screen 8 is numbered twice; Nfl (sNfL elsewhere); used in other rare neurological e.g. (word missing); A lack of objective data and Due to a lack reliable tools; clinician's face; Side effect of the drug or and worsening; a latter stage.
Appendix A · Scene map select to open
Scene 1 · screens 1, 2
Start. Title; How to use opens from a help button rather than as its own screen; time to complete.
Scene 2 · screens 3, 4
Overview. The contents become the menu, each scene ticked when done; learning objectives on the same screen.
Scene 3 · screens 5, 6, 7
Getting to know CIDP. The typical-symptom question with feedback per answer; then the variants ordering task and the reveal with figures.
Scene 4 · screen 8
The biomarker landscape. The four-era timeline, each era opened in turn; the closing points once all four are open. Follows PNS 2026 slide 22 (Q3).
Scene 5 · screens 9–17
The CIDP journey. One scene. The journey map is the navigation; the four stages unlock in order and can be revisited. Each stage: Consider (prompt; the patient vignette on stage 3) → Challenges, revealed one at a time → Your view, pick the hardest → Biomarker applications, with one scored question (S2) → Rank the benefits, then the payoff line (S3).
Scene 6 · screen 18
Your journey, summed up. Take-home messages beside the learner's own picks and rankings (S5); questions for clinicians to consider.
Scene 7 · screen 19
Sources and further reading. One panel, opened from any scene: numbered references, additional reading, registries.
